# Windows guest knobs

Every setting the Windows guest stack reads: the kernel driver's service-key values, the user-mode
drivers' `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Helios` values, the environment variables of the UMDs, bridges and our Mesa,
DXVK and vkd3d-proton patches, and the host's `conduit config` keys that shape what the guest sees.
Names, types, defaults and source lines come from the code; this page is regenerated and checked
in CI, so a default that changes in code changes here.

## Recommended configuration

**Recommended configuration = code defaults; no registry values need to be set.** Every knob below
defaults to the tested configuration when its value is absent. Values left over from a test (an A/B
row, a bisect) keep acting until deleted: to return a guest to the recommended configuration, delete
every value this page lists from both keys except the ones the installation writes (next section),
then reboot.

Classes:

- **Supported setting**: a choice a user may make (for example which ICD the desktop composes on).
- **Performance tuning**: changes speed or latency, not behaviour; the default is the measured best.
- **Debug / diagnostic**: tracing, logging, counters, kill switches for bisecting. Off in normal use.
- **Experiment, not for users**: a path under development or an A/B arm. Leave at the default.
- **State written by the driver**: values the KMD persists for itself; not settings.

| Location | Supported setting | Performance tuning | Debug / diagnostic | Experiment, not for users | State written by the driver | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| KMD: service key | 7 | 26 | 26 | 28 | 12 | 99 |
| UMDs and ICD policy: `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Helios` | 18 | 17 | 25 | 8 | 0 | 68 |
| Environment variables | 8 | 28 | 89 | 32 | 0 | 157 |
| All | 33 | 71 | 140 | 68 | 12 | 324 |

## What the installation writes

These are the only values an installation sets. Everything else on this page is absent after a clean
install, which means the code default.

| Key | Value | Data | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Helios` | `DwmIcd` | `String "nvk"` | [install.ps1:20](../guest/windows/packaging/windows/install.ps1#L20) |
| `service key\Parameters` | `SingleDeviceInstall` | `REG_DWORD 1` | [helios_kmd_render.inx:106](../guest/windows/kmd_render/helios_kmd_render.inx#L106) |
| `device key\Interrupt Management\MessageSignaledInterruptProperties` | `MSISupported` | `REG_DWORD 0` | [helios_kmd_render.inx:148](../guest/windows/kmd_render/helios_kmd_render.inx#L148) |
| `device key\Interrupt Management\MessageSignaledInterruptProperties` | `MessageNumberLimit` | `REG_DWORD 3` | [helios_kmd_render.inx:149](../guest/windows/kmd_render/helios_kmd_render.inx#L149) |

`install.ps1 -VenusDesktop` deletes `DwmIcd` instead (DWM then composes on Venus). The INF also writes
the display class values Windows needs to load the UMDs, the Vulkan and OpenGL ICDs
(`UserModeDriverName`, `VulkanDriverName`, `OpenGLDriverName`, ...); those are driver registration,
not knobs.

## KMD: service key

`HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\helios_kmd_render`, REG_DWORD. Read by the kernel driver (`helios_kmd_render.sys`); most are read again at every StartDevice, so `pnputil /restart-device` applies them, the rest need a reboot (the Read column says which).

### Counters and mirrors written by the driver

Besides the state values above, the KMD writes 774 counter and mirror values
(`*Eff` values of the knob in force, fault counters, stage and latency statistics) into the same
key. They are output, not settings: setting one has no effect, and the driver overwrites it.
[TRACING.md](TRACING.md) explains the ones used for diagnosis.

## UMDs and ICD policy: `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Helios`

Read by the D3D11/D3D12 user-mode drivers, their DXVK/vkd3d-proton bridges, the shared ICD policy (`protocol/include/helios_icd_policy.h`, also compiled into NVK) and the install scripts. 64-bit view, also from WoW64 processes. Read once per process unless the Read column says otherwise: a running process (DWM included) keeps what it started with.

### Supported setting (18)

| Name | Type | Default (code) | Read | Effect | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DesktopFollowsDwm` | REG_DWORD | `1` | once per process (ICD choice) | 1: while DWM composes on NVK (DwmIcd=nvk and its marker event exists) every other process goes to NVK too, and Icd and the built-in deny-list no longer apply; only NvkDenyList keeps a process on Venus. 0 turns this rule off. | `Nvk12AdmitBeforeRender` | REG_DWORD | `1 (on)` | once per process | With Nvk12EclSync=2: 1 queues an ExecuteCommandLists' admission event before its HE12 v4 packet, so the batch reaches NVK once everything before it on the context was submitted and three batches can be on the GPU; runtime waits before the ECL still hold it and signals after it still follow the work. 0 queues the admission after the packet, so a batch waits for its own packet's in-flight slot and two batches can be on the GPU. Counter EclAdmitBeforeRender. See [rm-fence-marker.md](../guest/windows/docs/rm-fence-marker.md#completion-hints). | [knobs12.rs:484](../guest/windows/umd12/src/knobs12.rs#L484) |
| `Nvk12EclFencePrefetch` | REG_DWORD | `1 (on)` | once per process | With Nvk12EclSync=2: 1 makes the queue's next ECL fence as soon as an ECL is admitted, so the next submission does not wait for the fence-create round trip; 0 makes each fence inline. | [knobs12.rs:514](../guest/windows/umd12/src/knobs12.rs#L514) |
| `Nvk12EclSpinUs` | REG_DWORD | `2000` | once per process | Microseconds the CPU-wait arm of Nvk12EclSync (value 1) polls the engine before it blocks; 0 blocks at once. Clamped to 50000. | [knobs12.rs:396](../guest/windows/umd12/src/knobs12.rs#L396) |
| `Nvk12EclSync` | REG_DWORD | `2` | once per process | How the D3D12 runtime's context is ordered behind NVK work: 2 an RM fence per ExecuteCommandLists that the KMD waits for before completing the packet (falls back to 0 without NVK and KMD support); 0 a UMD monitored fence signalled by a per-queue worker; 1 ExecuteCommandLists waits on the CPU until its work completed. ## Environment variables

Per-process: they act only on the process whose environment carries them (and its children). None needs to be set; the code defaults are the tested configuration. `unset` means the code tests for presence or a value and does nothing without it.

### Supported setting (8)

| Name | Default (code) | Read | Effect | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HELIOS_ICD` | `unset` | once per process | venus or nvk puts this process's D3D11, OpenGL (Zink) and Vulkan on that ICD, ahead of HKLM\SOFTWARE\Helios Icd, NvkAllowList and the deny-lists. Unset: the shared ICD policy decides. See [dwm-on-nvk.md](dwm-on-nvk.md). *Note: our code sets it for the process ("nvk"): [bridge_icd_backend.cpp:709](../guest/windows/umd_common/bridge/bridge_icd_backend.cpp#L709).* | [bridge_icd_backend.cpp:415](../guest/windows/umd_common/bridge/bridge_icd_backend.cpp#L415), [bridge_icd_backend.cpp:417](../guest/windows/umd_common/bridge/bridge_icd_backend.cpp#L417), [bridge_icd_backend.cpp:705](../guest/windows/umd_common/bridge/bridge_icd_backend.cpp#L705), +1 |
| `HELIOS_ICD12` | `unset` | once per process | venus or nvk puts this process's D3D12 on that ICD; it wins over HELIOS_ICD, Nvk12 and NvkDenyList12. Unset: the D3D12 policy (NVK unless denied). | [bridge_icd_backend.cpp:392](../guest/windows/umd_common/bridge/bridge_icd_backend.cpp#L392) |

| `NAK_IF_CONVERT` | `unset` | first shader compile (once per process) | On by default (unset or 1); 0 turns it off. After register allocation, NAK predicates small then/else blocks (8 instructions, or 12 for a then- and an else-block together) instead of branching around them, and drops the BSSY/BSYNC pair of a region left without branches. Does not change register counts. Part of the shader cache key. | [0060-nak-if-conversion-after-register-allocation-NAK_IF_C.patch:86](../guest/nvk-rm/patches-common/0060-nak-if-conversion-after-register-allocation-NAK_IF_C.patch#L86) |
| `NAK_IMM_CSE` | `unset` | first shader compile (once per process) | Unset: in compute shaders, a register copy of an immediate (needed when an instruction cannot take two immediates, such as an FFMA by two constants) serves the following uses of that immediate in its block, as long as each is at most 16 instructions after the previous one. 1 does it in every stage (it can cost occupancy in fragment and vertex shaders), 0 never. Part of the shader cache key. | [0057-nak-a-register-copy-of-an-immediate-serves-the-next-.patch:88](../guest/nvk-rm/patches-common/0057-nak-a-register-copy-of-an-immediate-serves-the-next-.patch#L88) |
| `NAK_OCC_TARGET` | `unset` | device creation (once per process) | On by default (unset or 1); 0 turns it off. Rematerialization in NAK's GPR spiller (cheap values such as constants, constant-buffer and constant-memory loads, thread/CTA IDs and short ALU chains are recomputed at reloads instead of going to local memory; constant-memory loads through a constant-buffer address reload with one LDG from a UGPR copy of the address) and a per-shader register target: after scheduling, NAK estimates the cost of spilling down to each lower register count that gives more warps per SM (workgroup and shared memory limits included) and uses the one with the best estimated gain, never one that needs more than a few memory spills or any inside a loop. A NAK_GPR_CAP for a stage overrides the target of that stage and then spills with rematerialization. Part of the shader cache key. | [0056-nak-rematerialization-and-per-shader-occupancy-targe.patch:198](../guest/nvk-rm/patches-common/0056-nak-rematerialization-and-per-shader-occupancy-targe.patch#L198) |
| `NAK_PHI_AVOID` | `unset` | first shader compile (once per process) | On by default (unset or 1); 0 turns it off. Register allocation keeps a new value without a register preference out of the registers that the phi copies at the end of its block want for other values, which saves copies and swaps at if/else merges. Part of the shader cache key. | [0062-nak-keep-new-values-out-of-the-registers-phi-copies-.patch:160](../guest/nvk-rm/patches-common/0062-nak-keep-new-values-out-of-the-registers-phi-copies-.patch#L160) |
| `NAK_PLOP_FOLD` | `unset` | first shader compile (once per process) | On by default (unset or 1); 0 turns it off. A PLOP3 that combines a comparison with one other predicate becomes the comparison's accumulator (FSETP/ISETP .AND/.OR/.XOR). Part of the shader cache key. | [0059-nak-a-PLOP3-of-a-comparison-and-a-predicate-becomes-.patch:68](../guest/nvk-rm/patches-common/0059-nak-a-PLOP3-of-a-comparison-and-a-predicate-becomes-.patch#L68) |
| `NAK_UADDR_PIN` | `unset` | first shader compile (once per process) | On by default (unset or 1); 0 turns it off. | `NVK_SKIP_DRAWID` | `false` | device creation | 1 skips writing the draw index for indirect draws (test only; wrong for shaders that read it); 0 writes it. | [0029-nvk-MME-budget-2976-checked-before-upload-mesh-macro.patch:175](../guest/nvk-rm/patches-common/0029-nvk-MME-budget-2976-checked-before-upload-mesh-macro.patch#L175) |

## Host: `conduit config` keys that shape the guest

Set on the host with `conduit config set KEY VALUE` ([CLI.md](CLI.md)); stored in
`~/.config/conduit/config.json`. The text is the key's own help from `cli/src/config.rs`.

| Key | Named values | What it does (default) |
|---|---|---|
| `view.close_stops_vm` | true, false | closing the window of a VM that `conduit view` started shuts it down (default true) |
| `venus.guest_blobs` | true, false | serve guest-memory blobs to Venus guests (the Windows KMD's windowed Present writes guest pages directly), from the next backend start (default false) |
| `backend.latency` | off, all | round-trip latency options for the backend and conduit-venus, from the next backend start (default all: quiet-held, fused-submit, direct-fences, event-batch; a comma-separated list sets exactly those, fence-spin included only when named) |
| `backend.cpus` | see text | keep the backend and conduit-venus on these host CPUs, from the next backend start (unset: any CPU; a list such as 0-7,16-23) |
| `backend.gpu_timeslice_us` | off, 0 | GPU timeslice of each guest channel group in microseconds, so host display work waits at most that long behind a busy guest, from the next backend start (default 100; off or 0: the driver's own 1024; also any number from 50 to 1024) |
| `host.isolation` | auto, off | keep host work, device interrupts and kernel workqueues off a running libvirt VM's CPUs, from its next start (default auto: CPUs from the VM's pinning and the CPU topology; off; or the VM's CPUs as a list such as 8-15,24-31) |
| `host.isolation.VM` | auto, off | host.isolation for the VM called VM (e.g. host.isolation.win11), from its next start (unset: host.isolation) |
| `viewer.gpu` | auto, dgpu, igpu | the GPU the viewer copies or scales frames on when the compositor does not take them as they are, from the viewer's next start (default auto: the GPU that made the frames; dgpu, igpu, or a render node such as /dev/dri/renderD128) |
| `viewer.gpu.VM` | auto, dgpu, igpu | viewer.gpu for the VM called VM (e.g. viewer.gpu.win11) (unset: viewer.gpu) |
| `gpu.vram_limit_mib` | auto, off | MiB of video memory a guest may hold, or off, from the next backend start (unset: a cap when safe mode is on and the NVIDIA card drives a monitor; auto: that cap whatever the driver; off: none; also any number of MiB) |
| `gpu.safe_mode` | auto, true, false | safe mode (CONDUIT_SAFE_MODE=1): a 2 GiB video-memory cap and 1 s blocking timeouts, from the next backend start (default auto: on for a driver Conduit is untested with, off for open modules 580 or newer) |
| `gpu.window_mib` | auto, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536, 131072, 262144 | MiB of shared window for guest CPU mappings of GPU memory, from the next backend start (default auto: the host GPU's BAR1) |

Background: [HOST-TUNING.md](HOST-TUNING.md) (`backend.gpu_timeslice_us`, `host.isolation`,
`backend.cpus`), [VIEWER.md](VIEWER.md) (`viewer.gpu`), [VENUS.md](VENUS.md) (`venus.guest_blobs`).
